chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, who said:

'Ali ibn Asbaat asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while we were listening: 'Is the twilight the redness or the whiteness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The redness. If it were the whiteness, it would be until the third of the night.'

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: Twilight, the glow in the sky after sunset

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between red and white twilight in Shia jurisprudence for Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the red twilight (shafaq al-ahmar) as the definitive marker for the end of Maghrib time, distinguishing it from the whiteness which extends later. The Imam’s explanation that whiteness would last until the third of the night provides a practical temporal boundary, reflecting the scholarly consensus on the precise moment for concluding the Maghrib prayer. This distinction is crucial for determining the start of the Isha time and aligns with the broader Shia jurisprudence on lunar phases and twilight definitions.
